subject: AP path clarification: card limits, vendor blocklist, and marketplace option
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Emma Clarke <emma@synergent.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick recap + procurement questions (PO vs card / marketplace)

Hi Emma — great chat this morning. Quick recap and a couple of follow-ups so we can confirm the right commercial path for the pilot: 

- Pilot goal: 3-week sandbox for engineering to validate latency/quality; estimated monthly spend ~$7k during pilot.
- Procurement constraints you mentioned: AP vendor onboarding + PO process could take multiple weeks; corporate card usage might be faster but you noted a $5k monthly card limit for third-party SaaS.
- Marketplace: you said Synergent is evaluating AWS Marketplace purchases for some vendors — curious whether Redwood can be on your marketplace vendor list (we can provide listing info and a pricing SKU).

Open items for your team: 
1) Is a vendor setup form required up front (vendor tax info, W9, bank details)?
2) If PO is required, what is the typical approval lead time (days)?
3) Is there flexibility to raise the card limit for a pilot or allow a one-off corporate card payment?

If it helps, I can loop in our finance ops lead (Karthik) to propose options: invoice w/ NET30, marketplace subscription, or card for pilot with an invoice afterwards. Attached is a short vendor onboarding checklist to speed things up if you want to start vendor setup.

Next steps: can you confirm which of the three routes (PO, card, marketplace) is feasible on your side and any paperwork we should pre-fill?

Thanks — Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0188
Redwood Inference

Attachment: Redwood_Vendor-Onboarding-Checklist.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Emma Clarke <emma@synergent.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Ops <procurement@synergent.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 08:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick recap + procurement questions (PO vs card / marketplace)

Hi Lauren — thanks for the recap. Quick answers from procurement: 

- Vendor setup: yes, we need a vendor form + W9 (standard). We can accept vendor paperwork before a PO is issued; it shortens the timeline once PO is raised.
- PO timeline: 2–4 weeks typical for standard SaaS (depending on legal review).
- Corporate card: our AP policy allows card payments up to $5k per month for third-party SaaS. Exceptions are rare and require VP Finance approval.
- Blocklist note: any vendor not in our vendor master requires additional vetting; last year we had a handful of blocked vendors due to IP/transfer restrictions.

Given your ~$7k pilot estimate, card would exceed the $5k policy. Two options we can consider: 
A) Approve a one-time exception (VP sign-off) — I can start that path if you can provide a short justification and evidence of vendor security posture (SOC2, data handling).
B) Purchase via AWS Marketplace if Redwood has a marketplace listing and pricing SKU — marketplace purchases bypass our direct vendor onboarding and are usually faster.

I'll attach the vendor form; fill it out and I can start vendor onboarding. If Redwood can share SOC2 Type II or equivalent security documentation, that will help with the exception route.

Best — Emma
Emma Clarke
Senior Procurement Manager, Synergent Labs
emma@synergent.com

Attachment: Synergent_Vendor_Form.pdf (pdf)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Quick recap + procurement questions (PO vs card / marketplace)

Looping Marissa from Finance Ops for suggested paths. Emma flagged two practical routes: 1) request VP exception to card limit (needs SOC2 and justification), or 2) do marketplace purchase.

Marissa — can we propose a short playbook for customers in this exact scenario (pilot > $5k/month, procurement slow): 
- Option 1: Marketplace SKU for fast onboarding (what do we need to publish?)
- Option 2: Short-term invoice (NET15) + vendor setup in parallel (what approvals does Redwood finance require to invoice without vendor master?)
- Option 3: One-off card exception (what documentation do we prepare to expedite VP approval?)

I'll attach the vendor form Emma sent.

Thanks,
Karthik

Attachment: Synergent_Vendor_Form.pdf (forwarded)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Emma Clarke <emma@synergent.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Apr 2027 07:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick recap + procurement questions (PO vs card / marketplace)

Hi Emma / team — thanks for the details. Two pragmatic proposals from finance to shorten time-to-value for the pilot: 

1) Marketplace route (preferred if you can accept it)
- What we need: confirmation you can purchase via AWS Marketplace and whether a single monthly subscription SKU is sufficient for your pilot. Redwood can prep a marketplace listing (takes ~7–12 business days to publish if we already have the paperwork with AWS).

2) Interim invoicing + vendor setup in parallel (backup)- Redwood can issue a proforma invoice for the pilot amount and accept payment via ACH once vendor onboarding completes. We can offer NET15 terms for pilot customers with legal-approved SOW. To do this we need: completed vendor form + PO when available OR a signed SOW + AR contact.

3) Card exception (fastest but needs VP sign-off)
- If Synergent is open to providing a short written justification for an exception (pilot critical to product roadmap, limited spend, will move to PO/marketplace post-validation), we can submit to our CFO for a one-time exception. Please include the SOC2 report link if available.

I've attached our vendor onboarding checklist and a simple pilot SOW template to accelerate legal. If you confirm marketplace is acceptable, Lauren and I will coordinate the AWS SKU and pricing. If not, please return the filled vendor form and we will prioritize vendor setup while invoicing the pilot.

Action items: 
- Emma: confirm marketplace OK or return vendor form (Synergent_Vendor_Form.pdf).
- Lauren: share pilot SOW with Emma (I attached template).

Best regards,
Marissa Cole
Head of Finance Ops | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 650-555-0124

Attachments: Redwood_Vendor-Onboarding-Checklist.xlsx, Pilot_SOW_Template.docx

From: Emma Clarke <emma@synergent.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Apr 2027 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick recap + procurement questions (PO vs card / marketplace)

Thanks everyone — we prefer the marketplace route if Redwood can get a listing in place quickly. Two quick asks from our side: 

1) Please share SOC2 Type II evidence (or equivalent) for vendor vetting.
2) If you can provide an AWS Marketplace SKU and a short pricing sheet for the pilot, I will route to our procurement contact and confirm purchase window.

I'll hold off on vendor form submission for now. If marketplace timelines look long, we'll send the vendor form and request an invoice while onboarding completes.

Appreciate the quick coordination.

— Emma
Emma Clarke
Senior Procurement Manager, Synergent Labs
procurement@synergent.com
